newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares hit another life high.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares hit another life high.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange jumped to its second record close in as many days on Thursday boosted by blue chips such as Kvaerner and Norsk Hydro .
The Oslo bourse hit an intra-day peak of 1,151.75 points. It then lost some ground but finished at 1,146.97 points, up 0.55 percent from Wednesday's record close.
Trade was heavy at 1.46 billion crowns.
Kvaerner, the anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group, was the most traded share at 247 million crowns. The A share closed 1.78 percent higher at 400 crowns.

Industrial conglomerate Hydro, Norway's largest listed company and with a 20 percent weighting on the Total index, climbed 1.11 percent to 364 crowns. It was the third most traded share at 159 million crowns.
Industrial holding group Aker RGI said it had sold 4.2 million shares in Norway Seafoods at 50 crowns per share to a consortium of Norwegian institutional investors.

The transaction made Norway Seafoods the second most traded share at 216 million crowns, leaving its price unchanged. Aker RGI has thus sold half the shares it took over from U.S. fund Tiger Management last week as part of an option deal.
